Q: What is the way to verify beforehand if a function works for any version of java jre? A:

Check the class's Javadoc. In this case, the class is noted as being present "since JDK1.1", and the method doesn't have a more specific date, so anything since Java 1.1 should support it.

Q: Misspecifying a parameter in min()/max() does not throw an error or warning. Why? A:

Another base function that does not warn when trying to set a non-existent parameter is sum, for the reasons pointed by @jared_mamrot and @Steve. This is a general rule, after the dots argument all arguments must be named. And since min, max or sum have dots as their first argument, what follows must match the argument name exactly.

Q: How to mock MUI5 Pro license key in Jest tests for React components A:

Within the jest setup file, mock the MUI license returns. This should remove those console errors shown while testing with jest:

jest.mock('@mui/x-license-pro', () => ({
    ...jest.requireActual('@mui/x-license-pro'),
    useLicenseVerifier: () => 'Valid',
    Watermark: () => null,
})):

Alternatively, mocking this in your test suite's beforeAll(() => {}) also works if you don't need to mock it for all tests

Update May 2026

MUI X v7+ license module is located at '@mui/x-license' instead of '@mui/x-license-*', so will need to modify the above example accordingly
